title: DCP Pretty Good Measurement (PGM) Gram Eigenvalue Spectrum and Square-Root Occupancy Bridge
claims: The Q x Q secret Gram matrix G(A) has exact Fourier eigenvalues lambda_y(G(A)) = (Q / 2^K) * N_A(y) where N_A(y) is the subset-sum occupancy count mod q.
The exact PGM secret-recovery probability is P_{PGM}(A) = (sum_y sqrt(N_A(y)))^2 / (2^K * Q) <= R(A) / Q, with equality iff N_A(y) is constant across all R(A) occupied residues.
